name: Xiaohuanxiong (小浣熊) noodles
blurb: Uni-President's crunchy snack noodles with collectible Water Margin hero cards
title: Xiaohuanxiong (小浣熊) Noodles and Water Margin Cards
description: Xiaohuanxiong ("Little Raccoon") is Uni-President's crunchy snack noodle from 1994, famous for its 114 collectible Water Margin hero cards in the late 1990s.
answer: Xiaohuanxiong ("Little Raccoon") is a crunchy instant-noodle snack from Uni-President, launched in China in 1994 and eaten dry straight from the bag; in the 1990s it cost 0.5 yuan. It is remembered above all for the cards packed inside, especially the late-1990s Water Margin hero series: 114 cards, the novel's 108 heroes plus 6 villains. The noodles are still sold, and the cards have returned as a mobile game and a crowdfunded art project.

body: Think of a block of fried instant noodles sold as a snack, not a meal. You crushed the block inside the bag, tipped in the seasoning sachet, held the top shut and shook, then ate it by the handful. The bag showed a cartoon raccoon.

Tucked inside was a trading card. The famous series showed heroes from the classic novel Water Margin, drawn in a style mixing Chinese ink painting and Japanese manga by five artists working with an advertising agency. New cards were released a few at a time each month, in both Xiaohuanxiong and Uni-President's sister brand Xiaodangjia.

body: Yes. Uni-President still sells Xiaohuanxiong noodles, and has issued retro-style packaging. The original Water Margin cards no longer come in the bags; old ones circulate among collectors, and new versions exist only as separate games and art projects.

ul: Squeezing bags in the shop to feel for a card
Kids who bought the noodles for the card and threw the noodles away
Hardly anyone ever completing all 108 heroes

faq.q: How many Water Margin cards were there?
faq.a: 114: the 108 heroes of the novel plus 6 villains.
Uni-President, the Taiwanese food group, which launched them in mainland China in 1994.

faq.q: Why did the Water Margin card craze end?
faq.a: From 2002 complete sets were sold directly in shops, which took the fun out of collecting.
